title: atlas-findings block
description: What a producer puts in the ```atlas-findings fenced block of a route output. This is input to the checker, not an emitted atlas-finding.v1 document, and the difference matters: a producer supplies neither finding_id (derived from the claim and scope), nor verdict, nor verification_method. Those are assigned by whatever checked the finding, so a producer cannot declare its own success.

severity_rationale.description: A severity without a reason is a number someone can quote back as though it were assessed.

evidence.description: What the finding CLAIMS about its sources, checked against the run's observations rather than copied from them.

claim_check.description: A free-standing test of a free-text finding. Settling it settles the TEST, not the claim: nothing checks that the test is a fair test of the sentence, which is why its results are named condition_supported and condition_refuted and can never produce a verdict or reach PASS. A false claim beside a condition that holds stays insufficient_evidence, and a true claim beside a condition that fails is not called contradicted. For a strong verdict, use typed_claim instead.

kind.description: Literal text only. A producer-supplied regular expression is untrusted input that can hang the checker; a substring search cannot.

source_id.description: Must be a source this finding cites, and one the run read.

text.description: Empty would match everything and settle nothing.

typed_claim.description: A claim stated so that settling it settles the claim: text, source and scope are one object, not three independently chosen ones. This is the ONLY route to a verdict of verified or contradicted. The finding's `claim` string must equal the sentence derived from this object — 'PATH lines A-B contain "TEXT"' or '... do not contain ...' — so the sentence a reader sees cannot say more than what was tested. Settled against the lines the observation recorded, never the whole file. Mutually exclusive with claim_check: a typed claim is already its own test, and a second one beside it could only disagree.

source_id.description: Must be a source this finding cites, and one the run read.

text.description: Literal text. A producer-supplied regular expression is untrusted input that can hang the checker; a substring search cannot.
